introduction_markdown: Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Physics, Paper 2 (subject code 0580). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**EITHER 8 (a), (b) and (c)**

Define: (i) Electrostatic force. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Friction. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) An **electrostatic force** is the force of attraction or repulsion between electrically charged bodies: like charges repel and unlike charges attract.

(ii) **Friction** is the force that opposes the relative motion (or the tendency to move) between two surfaces in contact.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A student was investigating the acceleration of a small toy car down a run way using different forces. The data collected was as shown in the table below.

| F/N | 0.0 | 2.0 | 4.0 | 6.0 | 8.0 | 12.0 | 16.0 | 18.0 | 20.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a/m s$^{-2}$ | 0.0 | 1.6 | 3.4 | 5.2 | 7.0 | 10.6 | 14.2 | 16.0 | 18.0 |

(i) Define acceleration. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Plot a graph of F/N (y-axis) against a/m s$^{-2}$ (x-axis). *[5 marks]*

(iii) Determine the slope of the graph. *[2 marks]*

(iv) What physical quantity does the slope represent? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Acceleration** is the rate of change of velocity: $a = \dfrac{v-u}{t}$. Its SI unit is $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

(ii) **Graph.** Draw the axes with the acceleration $a$ ($\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$) on the horizontal axis, from $0$ to $20$ (for example $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ for $2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$), and the force $F$ (N) on the vertical axis, from $0$ to $20$ (for example $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ for $2\,\mathrm{N}$). Label the axes with their units and give the graph a title. Plot the nine points $(0,0)$, $(1.6,2.0)$, $(3.4,4.0)$, $(5.2,6.0)$, $(7.0,8.0)$, $(10.6,12.0)$, $(14.2,16.0)$, $(16.0,18.0)$, $(18.0,20.0)$ with small crosses. The points lie on a **straight line** going up to the right, almost through the origin: draw the best-fit straight line with a ruler so that the points are evenly spread on both sides.

(iii) Take a large triangle on the line, for example between $(1.6,\,2.0)$ and $(18.0,\,20.0)$:

slope $= \dfrac{\Delta F}{\Delta a} = \dfrac{20.0 - 2.0}{18.0 - 1.6} = \dfrac{18.0}{16.4} \approx 1.1\,\mathrm{N\,s^{2}\,m^{-1}} = 1.1\,\mathrm{kg}$.

(Values from about $1.0$ to $1.2$ are acceptable for a good graph.)

(iv) Since $F = ma$, the slope $\dfrac{F}{a} = m$ represents the **mass of the toy car** (about $1.1\,\mathrm{kg}$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
A motorist accelerates uniformly from rest and attains a velocity of $30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in $20\,\mathrm{s}$. He then continues with this velocity for a further $20\,\mathrm{s}$. He sees a child crossing the road $500\,\mathrm{m}$ away, and applies the brakes. This brings the car to rest in a further $15\,\mathrm{s}$.

(i) Sketch a velocity-time graph for the motion, indicating important values on both axes. *[3 marks]*

(ii) Show by calculation whether or not the motorist hits the child. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Draw $v$ ($\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$) on the vertical axis and $t$ (s) on the horizontal axis. The graph has three parts: a straight line from $(0,0)$ up to $(20,\,30)$ (uniform acceleration); a horizontal line at $v = 30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from $t = 20\,\mathrm{s}$ to $t = 40\,\mathrm{s}$ (constant velocity); a straight line down from $(40,\,30)$ to $(55,\,0)$ (uniform deceleration, the car stops $15\,\mathrm{s}$ later). Mark $30$ on the velocity axis and $20$, $40$, $55$ on the time axis. *(The sketch is made by the candidate.)*

(ii) The child is seen after the $20\,\mathrm{s}$ of constant velocity, when the brakes are applied. Braking distance = area of the triangle under the last part of the graph:

$s = \dfrac{1}{2}\times 15\times 30 = 225\,\mathrm{m}$.

Since $225\,\mathrm{m} < 500\,\mathrm{m}$, the car stops $500 - 225 = 275\,\mathrm{m}$ before the child: the motorist **does not hit the child**.

(Assumption: the child is $500\,\mathrm{m}$ ahead of the car at the instant the brakes are applied, and the reaction time is neglected.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
**OR 8 (d), (e) and (f)**

(i) State Ohm's law. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Define resistance and state its SI units. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Ohm's law:** the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it, provided the temperature and other physical conditions stay constant.

(ii) **Resistance** of a conductor is the ratio of the potential difference across it to the current flowing through it: $R = \dfrac{V}{I}$. Its SI unit is the **ohm** ($\Omega$), where $1\,\Omega = 1\,\mathrm{V\,A^{-1}}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A student wanted to investigate Ohm's law using a piece of copper wire. She measured the p.d. across the wire, and the current through it, and got the following results:

| p.d./V | 0.0 | 1.0 | 1.5 | 2.0 | 3.0 | 4.5 | 6.0 | 8.0 | 10.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I/A | 0.0 | 0.08 | 0.13 | 0.17 | 0.25 | 0.38 | 0.51 | 0.68 | 0.89 |

(i) Name the instrument used to measure the current and say how it is connected to the copper wire. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Plot a graph of p.d. (y-axis) against I (x-axis). *[5 marks]*

(iii) Determine the slope of your graph. *[2 marks]*

(iv) What physical quantity does the slope represent? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) An **ammeter**, connected in **series** with the copper wire.

(ii) **Graph.** Put the current $I$ (A) on the horizontal axis, from $0$ to $1.0$ (for example $2\,\mathrm{cm}$ for $0.1\,\mathrm{A}$), and the p.d. $V$ (V) on the vertical axis, from $0$ to $11$ (for example $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ for $1\,\mathrm{V}$). Label the axes with their units. Plot the nine points $(0,0)$, $(0.08,1.0)$, $(0.13,1.5)$, $(0.17,2.0)$, $(0.25,3.0)$, $(0.38,4.5)$, $(0.51,6.0)$, $(0.68,8.0)$, $(0.89,10.5)$. They lie on a **straight line through the origin**: draw the best-fit line with a ruler.

(iii) Take a large triangle on the line, for example between the origin and $(0.89\,\mathrm{A},\,10.5\,\mathrm{V})$: slope $= \dfrac{\Delta V}{\Delta I} = \dfrac{10.5 - 0}{0.89 - 0} \approx 11.8\,\Omega$ (values from about $11.5$ to $12.0\,\Omega$ are acceptable).

(iv) The slope $\dfrac{V}{I}$ represents the **resistance** of the copper wire (about $11.8\,\Omega$). The straight line through the origin shows that $V \propto I$, so the wire obeys Ohm's law.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An earth wire is considered as a safety precaution in house wiring.

(i) What does it protect? *[1 mark]*

(ii) Explain how the protection in (i) above is ensured. *[2 marks]*

(iii) A coffee maker is rated $2200\,\mathrm{W}$, $240\,\mathrm{V}$. A student brought a $5\,\mathrm{A}$ fuse to use on the coffee maker. Calculate the maximum current that flows in the coffee maker, and hence determine whether or not the $5\,\mathrm{A}$ fuse is suitable for use in the appliance. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) It protects the **user** (from electric shock) and the appliance (and the house wiring from fire).

(ii) The earth wire connects the metal casing of the appliance to the ground. If a fault makes the live wire touch the casing, a **large current flows through the earth wire to the ground** instead of through the user. This large current **melts (blows) the fuse** and cuts off the supply, and the casing is kept at (nearly) zero potential, so nobody receives a shock.

(iii) $P = IV$, so $I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{2200}{240} \approx 9.2\,\mathrm{A}$.

The current of $9.2\,\mathrm{A}$ is greater than $5\,\mathrm{A}$, so the $5\,\mathrm{A}$ fuse would **blow** every time the coffee maker is used: it is **not suitable**. A fuse of slightly higher rating than $9.2\,\mathrm{A}$, such as a $13\,\mathrm{A}$ fuse, should be used.
